title: Two paths
concept: Commits on two branches; the graph splits

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: Let's add the map file to our `map` branch.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: Wait, Sam just added an emergency fix to `main` while you were working!

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: Now our branch and `main` have split into two paths. Make your commit and watch the graph.

items.text: Add and commit map.html on the map branch

hints: You are on the map branch. Create a file, stage it, and commit.
Use `echo` or the editor to create map.html, then `git add` and `git commit`.
Type `echo "map" > map.html`, then `git add map.html` and `git commit -m "Add map"`.

predict.question: You are on the map branch. What will happen to the graph when you commit?

choices.text: The commit is added to the map branch, creating a split.

predict.explanation: Commits always go to your current branch (HEAD). The graph splits into two paths from the common ancestor.

recap: Branches allow you to work on an idea while the main branch continues to receive updates.
